domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and optional cancellation. References Employee (via employeeId) and LeavePolicy (via leaveTypeId).
lifecycle_states: DRAFT: Initial state when an employee begins but has not yet submitted a leave request. Editable by the employee. No balance impact.
SUBMITTED: Employee has formally submitted the request for manager review. Employee cannot edit. Awaiting manager action.
APPROVED: Manager has approved the request. Balance is deducted. Terminal positive state.
REJECTED: Manager has rejected the request. No balance impact. Terminal negative state.
CANCELLED: Request was withdrawn by the employee (from DRAFT or SUBMITTED) or cancelled after approval (from APPROVED, subject to constraints). Balance is restored if previously deducted.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of all possible lifecycle states for a LeaveRequest. Drives state-transition guards and query filtering.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Each policy governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether accrual applies, notice requirements, and whether manager approval is mandatory. Referenced by LeaveBalance and LeaveRequest.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Policy is in effect and governs new leave requests and balance calculations.
INACTIVE: Policy has been retired. Existing balances and approved requests under this policy remain valid, but no new requests may be submitted against it.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type may have distinct policies, balance tracking, and approval rules. The feature scope explicitly covers ANNUAL, SICK, and EMERGENCY; the remaining types are defined for completeness.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific LeavePolicy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when a leave request is approved (usedDays increases, remainingDays decreases) or when an approved request is cancelled (usedDays decreases, remainingDays increases).
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Balance is in effect for the current fiscal year. Accruals and deductions apply.
EXHAUSTED: remainingDays has reached zero. No further leave of this type can be approved unless the policy allows negative balances (unpaid leave).
CLOSED: Fiscal year has ended. Balance is frozen; no further deductions or accruals. A new balance record is created for the next fiscal year.

domain_entities.name: BalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of LeaveBalance lifecycle states. Drives whether deductions are permitted and whether the balance is current.

business_rules: LeaveRequest state transitions: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (employee submits), DRAFT → CANCELLED (employee discards draft), SUBMITTED → APPROVED (manager approves), SUBMITTED → REJECTED (manager rejects), SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (employee withdraws pending request), APPROVED → CANCELLED (employee cancels approved leave; balance is restored). No other transitions are valid. Once in REJECTED or CANCELLED, the request is terminal and cannot be reopened. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]
startDate must be on or before endDate. A leave request with startDate after endDate is invalid at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to APPROVED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays must be incremented by the leave duration in days, and LeaveBalance.remainingDays decremented by the same amount. This deduction is atomic with the status transition. If remainingDays would become negative and the LeavePolicy does not permit negative balances (i.e. leaveType is not UNPAID), the approval must be rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the corresponding LeaveBalance.usedDays must be decremented by the leave duration in days, and LeaveBalance.remainingDays incremented by the same amount. This restoration is atomic with the status transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee cannot submit a leave request that overlaps in dates with an existing APPROVED or SUBMITTED leave request for the same employee. Overlap is defined as two date ranges [startDate, endDate] that share at least one calendar day. DRAFT and REJECTED requests are excluded from overlap checks. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Only the employee's designated manager (Employee.managerId) or a user with the MANAGER role may approve or reject a SUBMITTED LeaveRequest. An employee cannot approve or reject their own leave request. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

If LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set and greater than zero, the number of calendar days between the submission date and the leave startDate must be at least minimumNoticeDays. Requests that violate this must be rejected at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

LeaveBalance.remainingDays is a derived invariant: remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays. It must never be set independently; it is always computed from the other two fields. Any code that writes to remainingDays directly (outside of the atomic deduction/restoration operations) is invalid. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When LeaveBalance.remainingDays reaches zero, the balance transitions from ACTIVE to EXHAUSTED. When a new fiscal year begins, all ACTIVE and EXHAUSTED balances for that year transition to CLOSED, and new ACTIVE balances are created for the new fiscal year based on the policy's entitlementDays (and any carryover rules, if defined). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

A LeavePolicy with isActive = false (INACTIVE) cannot be used for new LeaveRequest submissions. Existing approved requests and balances under an inactive policy remain valid and unaffected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

Only the employee who owns the LeaveRequest (employeeId) may submit a DRAFT, or cancel a SUBMITTED request. Only a manager may approve or reject. Cancellation of an APPROVED request may be performed by either the employee or their manager, but if the leave startDate has already passed, cancellation may be restricted (see open question on past-date cancellation). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee with employmentStatus INACTIVE or TERMINATED cannot create or submit a LeaveRequest. Only ACTIVE employees are eligible to apply for leave. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Every state-changing operation on a LeaveRequest (submit, approve, reject, cancel) must produce an audit record (GP-002). The audit record must capture: entityType='LeaveRequest', entityId, action matching the transition, oldValues (previous status), newValues (new status), performedBy (the actor's employeeId), and performedAt. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

When a LeaveBalance transitions to CLOSED (fiscal year end), if the policy has maxAccumulation set and remainingDays > 0, the carryover amount into the new fiscal year's balance is min(remainingDays, maxAccumulation). If maxAccumulation is null, no carryover occurs (use-it-or-lose-it). The new fiscal year balance's totalEntitlement = policy.entitlementDays + carryoverAmount. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest transitions to SUBMITTED, a notification must be created for the employee's manager (recipientId = Employee.managerId) with type='LEAVE_REQUEST_SUBMITTED'. When a manager approves or rejects, a notification must be created for the employee with type='LEAVE_REQUEST_APPROVED' or 'LEAVE_REQUEST_REJECTED'. Notification creation is part of the same atomic operation as the status transition. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Emergency leave (leaveType = EMERGENCY) bypasses the minimumNoticeDays check. The notice period requirement is waived for emergency leave requests regardless of the LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays value. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED | REJECTED; DRAFT → CANCELLED; SUBMITTED → CANCELLED; APPROVED → CANCELLED. REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal.
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE ↔ INACTIVE (toggle via isActive flag).
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED (when remainingDays hits 0); ACTIVE | EXHAUSTED → CLOSED (fiscal year rollover).

## Key business rules (broad scope)

- BR: startDate ≤ endDate always.
- BR: Balance deduction on APPROVED; restoration on CANCELLED (from APPROVED). Both atomic with status transition.
- BR: No overlapping APPROVED/SUBMITTED requests for same employee.
- BR: Only designated manager (or MANAGER role) may approve/reject; employee cannot self-approve.
- BR: minimumNoticeDays enforced at submission (waived for EMERGENCY leave).
- BR: remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays (invariant; never set independently).
- BR: INACTIVE employees cannot apply; INACTIVE policies cannot be used for new requests.
- BR: Fiscal year rollover: carryover = min(remainingDays, maxAccumulation) if maxAccumulation is set; otherwise zero.
- BR: Audit records (GP-002) and notifications produced on every state transition.

## Open questions for chief architect

1. Day counting semantics (inclusive/exclusive, calendar/business days) — affects all balance arithmetic.
2. Post-startDate cancellation of APPROVED leave — allowed? prorated?
3. Fiscal year definition — calendar, configurable company year, or per-employee anniversary?

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted from startDate and endDate? Specifically: (a) inclusive or exclusive of the end date, and (b) calendar days or business/working days? The answer affects balance deduction arithmetic, minimum-notice calculations, and sufficiency checks everywhere.
open_questions.impact: Every balance deduction, sufficiency check, and notice-period validation depends on this. An inconsistent choice across call sites would produce the BR-001 anti-pattern.

open_questions.question: Can an APPROVED leave request be cancelled after its startDate has already passed (or partially passed)? If so, how is the balance restoration calculated — full days, only remaining future days, or prorated?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance restoration logic and whether the CANCELLED transition from APPROVED needs a date guard. Without a decision, the system could restore days for leave already taken.
candidate_options: No cancellation after startDate — once leave begins, it cannot be undone
Full cancellation allowed — all days restored regardless of startDate
Prorated cancellation — only future (unused) days are restored to balance

open_questions.question: How is the fiscal year defined for LeaveBalance? Is it calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), a configurable company fiscal year (e.g. Apr 1 – Mar 31), or per-employee based on hire date anniversary?
open_questions.impact: Determines when balances roll over, when CLOSED transitions fire, and how entitlement is allocated. Affects the fiscalYear field semantics and the rollover job design.
candidate_options: Per-employee anniversary year based on hireDate
